title: Query attempt logging (foundational)
description: Every retrieval attempt is logged with the query text, the strategy used, result count, and whether the user engaged with the results. The log is the raw material for all learning; without it, the system repeats the same failed queries forever. Logs are compact structured rows, cheap to store by the millions. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
log = []
def attempt(q, strategy, hits, engaged):
    log.append({'q': q, 'strategy': strategy, 'hits': hits, 'engaged': engaged})
attempt('index latency', 'keyword', 12, True)
attempt('fast search', 'keyword', 0, False)
print('logged attempts:', len(log))
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Retrieval History Analyzer practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Per-strategy success scoring (foundational)
description: Each strategy's success rate is its engaged-attempts over total attempts, with Laplace smoothing so new strategies start at a neutral prior instead of zero. Smoothed rates let the analyzer compare a battle-tested strategy against a newcomer fairly. The scores feed directly into strategy selection for future queries. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.

title: Failure pattern mining (foundational)
description: Failed attempts are grouped by shared features: query length, presence of rare terms, strategy used. Recurring failure patterns become explicit rules, such as 'single-term queries fail under the semantic strategy'. Mining turns anecdotes about bad searches into actionable fixes. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
from collections import Counter
fails = [('fast search', 'semantic'), ('quick lookup', 'semantic'), ('index latency', 'keyword')]
pat = Counter(s for _, s in fails)
print('failure by strategy:', dict(pat))
print('pattern: semantic strategy failing on short queries')

title: Query reformulation recommendation (foundational)
description: When a query fails, the analyzer recommends the closest historically successful query by edit distance, biased toward queries from the same topic. Recommendation reuses what worked instead of asking the user to guess better phrasing. The suggested query is shown with its historical success rate as justification. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
def lev(a, b):
    dp = list(range(len(b) + 1))
    for i, ca in enumerate(a, 1):
        ndp = [i]
        for j, cb in enumerate(b, 1):
            ndp.append(min(dp[j] + 1, ndp[-1] + 1, dp[j-1] + (ca != cb)))
        dp = ndp
    return dp[-1]
winners = ['index latency tuning', 'posting list optimization']
q = 'index latncy'
print('try instead:', min(winners, key=lambda w: lev(q, w)))
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Retrieval History Analyzer practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Strategy feedback loop (foundational)
description: Success scores flow back into the live retriever: the strategy picker weights each strategy by its smoothed success rate, re-normalized after every batch of attempts. The loop is closed and automatic, so retrieval improves with use instead of stagnating at its initial tuning. A floor weight keeps every strategy sampled occasionally, preventing premature convergence. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Retrieval History Analyzer practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.
